title: How Many Trips?
idea: When every truck load is the same size, the trips needed is how many loads fit the pile, and a part load left over still needs a whole trip.

serves.objective: SCI005-02-d: estimate how many full truck loads it takes to move a pile when every load is the same size, then check by hauling

haul.title: Haul the pile
haul.scene: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 90' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='0' y='70' width='320' height='20' fill='#44403c'/><polygon points='8,70 40,38 72,70' fill='#92400e'/><text x='40' y='84' font-size='10' fill='#e2e8f0' text-anchor='middle'>pile</text><rect x='280' y='60' width='34' height='10' fill='#a16207'/><text x='297' y='84' font-size='10' fill='#e2e8f0' text-anchor='middle'>dump</text><g data-bind='trips' data-move='24,0'><text x='78' y='68' font-size='26'>🚚</text><g data-bind='holds' data-move='0,-2'><ellipse cx='94' cy='48' rx='9' ry='4' fill='#92400e'/></g></g><g data-bind='gone' data-show='yes'><text x='160' y='18' fill='#34d399' font-size='13' text-anchor='middle'>The pile is gone!</text></g><g data-bind='gone' data-show='no'><text x='160' y='18' fill='#f87171' font-size='13' text-anchor='middle'>Some dirt is left</text></g></svg>

draft.prompt: The truck carries the same load every trip. Set the trips so the whole pile is hauled away, with no extra trip.

help.says: Each trip takes one full load. Count on by the truck load for every trip.

simplify.says: I set some of the trips for you.

draft.why: The child counts a pile in truck loads, not scoops, on a pile that is an exact number of loads.

draft.prompt: A new pile of {{pile2}} scoops. Before the truck goes: what is the fewest trips that moves the whole pile?

help.says: Count by the truck load until you reach the pile or go past it. A little dirt left over still needs a trip.

draft.why: The child commits a trip count before hauling; this pile leaves a part load, so the last trip is the one children miss.

draft.prompt: Now haul it. Set the trips for the pile of {{pile2}}, with no extra trip.

help.says: After the full loads, look at what is left in the pile. Does it need one more trip?

simplify.says: I set the trips for all the full loads. Run it and look at the pile.

draft.why: The prediction played out on the same truck: the run shows the dirt left after the full loads, the misconception's own result.

draft.prompt: A pile of {{pile3}} scoops and only {{t4}} trips before dark. Change the truck instead: use the smallest truck load that clears the pile in {{t4}} trips.

help.says: With the trips fixed, a bigger load means more dirt each trip. Count by the load {{t4}} times.

simplify.says: I made the truck bigger part of the way.

draft.why: The other side of the same model: when the trips are fixed, the load size has to change, and a bigger load means fewer trips.
